name: Pinochle Single Deck Partnership
description: Pinochle with single 48-card deck; four players in partnerships. Melding and trick-taking.

content.text: Pinochle with single 48-card deck; four players in partnerships. Melding and trick-taking.

Partnership pinochle shares the same roots as pinochle generally: either as a cousin of Binokel with both evolving from bezique, or from the Swiss and South German game Binocle or Binokel. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where it was mispronounced and misspelled as 'pinochle'; it became a favorite among American Jewish and Irish immigrants. Partnership auction pinochle emerged as the standard form in the United States in the early 20th century.
48-card Pinochle deck: twelve cards per suit (two each of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace) in all four French suits.
Standard 48-card Pinochle deck (two copies of 9 through Ace in each suit).
All 48 cards dealt clockwise in packets of three or four, starting with the player to the dealer's left (eldest hand). Each player receives 12 cards. Deal rotates clockwise each hand.
